objects.description: Time the knowledge stages, then remove the per-file subprocesses in discovery and extraction so that nodes and edges take one pass per source.

objects.title: The test runner reports per-case time and the suite budget
objects.description: Print each case's wall time in test/run.sh, sort the slowest at the end, and record the suite's total in the benchmark history as a system target.

objects.title: CI runs the structural performance checks
objects.description: Add the flatten-once case, the cache-equivalence case and bench --check with the CI profile to validate.yml, with the wall-clock thresholds conservative and the counters exact.

objects.title: A synthetic repository generator for scaling cases
objects.description: Add a test helper that builds a repository with N issues, N milestones, N rules and N context documents from the skeleton, and a case that runs doctor and plan validate at three sizes and asserts the yaml_flatten count grows linearly.

objects.title: Timing report as JSON
objects.description: Under --json, print the timing report as one JSON object on stderr with phases and counters, so bench can carry a phase breakdown per sample.

objects.title: bench compare and the top regressions report
objects.description: Add bench compare <run-a> <run-b> and make the human report rank the largest regressions, the largest improvements and the slowest targets by p95.

objects.title: watch inherits every doctor fix and its own budget
objects.description: Confirm watch dispatches the rewritten validators, time it, and declare benchmark.budget.watch_ms next to doctor's.

objects.title: context and its subcommands under a second
objects.description: Time context resolve, validate, affected and check-sync, and remove the per-document git and awk calls so each runs under a second on this repository.

objects.title: Cache equivalence proved by property-shaped cases
objects.description: For every read-only command in the registry, run it with the cache cold, warm, and disabled, on this repository and on a synthetic one, and assert byte-identical output and exit code; then mutate one file and assert the changed output is served.

objects.title: Before and after evidence for every optimisation
objects.description: Record, for each hot spot removed, the phase time before and after and the counter before and after, in the benchmark history and in the commit message, and summarise them in docs/PERFORMANCE.md by pointing at the baseline file.

objects.title: The performance workflow is discoverable and complete
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion of M004 has evidence, the README workflow runs as written, the site is regenerated, and the final report is a plan record rather than a conversation.

objects.title: The deployment description is a kind of the layer, not a provider file
objects.description: Register `deployment` as a kind of the AI layer — allowed keys, schema, directory contract — and describe this repository's own deployment as one object under .ai/repo/deployments/, so that every later projection reads one file and no provider file is ever authoritative.

objects.title: The deployment object becomes typed Rust that refuses nonsense
objects.description: Parse the canonical deployment object into strongly typed Rust — enums and newtypes rather than strings — and validate it so that a deployment that cannot work is refused before anything is built.

objects.title: Deployment reads are declared once and projected everywhere
objects.description: Declare the read-only deployment operations as canonical capabilities so that the CLI, the HTTP API, MCP, OpenAPI and the generated documentation all derive from one declaration.

objects.title: The listen address is one fact with two projections
objects.description: Make the deployment bind an externally reachable interface on the port the canonical object declares, without changing the loopback default that local use depends on, and without the port existing as a literal in more than one place.

objects.title: Liveness and readiness are registered capabilities, not router hacks
objects.description: Expose cheap liveness and readiness endpoints through the capability registry, so that the provider health check, the container test and the smoke suite all point at routes the registry knows about.

objects.title: Termination is graceful and proved against the real container
objects.description: Handle SIGTERM and SIGINT so that a Machine that is being stopped, redeployed or autostopped finishes its in-flight responses and exits inside the platform's timeout.

objects.title: The running process says what it is, from an allowlist
objects.description: Expose the version, revision, build profile, target and the safe platform facts of a hosted process through the existing metadata surface, with every field explicitly allowlisted.

objects.title: A hosted process has no repository, and says so instead of failing
objects.description: Separate the local mode that inspects a developer's repository from the hosted mode that serves a packaged layer, and report the capabilities that are unavailable in hosted mode from capability metadata rather than from a hand-written list.

objects.title: The production image is a generated projection of the build specification
objects.description: Generate a multi-stage container build and its ignore file from the deployment object's build specification: a pinned Alpine runtime holding the binary, the runtime assets and nothing else, executed by an unprivileged user.

objects.title: The release profile is chosen by measurement, not by folklore
objects.description: Measure the size, startup, memory and latency consequences of the candidate release configurations and select the smallest one that does not regress runtime behaviour materially, recording the decision and the numbers.

objects.title: A source change does not rebuild the world, and the context stays small
objects.description: Make the container build reuse dependency layers and caches so that a source-only change does not rebuild every dependency, and keep the build context to the inputs the deployment object declares.

objects.title: The image serves the site the canonical pipeline produced
objects.description: Build the served documentation and site assets in the container with the same pipeline local development and the Pages deployment already use, and carry exactly those outputs into the runtime stage.

objects.title: The provider configuration is generated, and the cheap profile is declared
objects.description: Generate the Fly configuration from the canonical object — application, region, port, resources, autostart and autostop, health check, concurrency — and declare the cheap cost profile as data that a reader and a check can both see.

objects.title: One deployment core, one command, and a dry run that mutates nothing
objects.description: Implement the deployment operations — validate, plan, generate, build, status, deploy, smoke — once in the typed core, expose them through thin adapters, and provide one ergonomic command that performs the whole sequence safely and can be asked to change nothing.

objects.title: Deployment joins the diagnostics that already exist
objects.description: Add the deployment checks to the health and doctor architecture the repository already has, so that the answer to whether a deployment can succeed comes from the same diagnostic surface as every other verdict.

objects.title: The smoke suite is derived from the route registry, never written twice
objects.description: Generate the deployment smoke tests from the authoritative route registry, extending route metadata only where smoke testing genuinely needs it, and cover the surfaces that a plain status code cannot verify.

objects.title: A bad deployment can be undone deterministically
objects.description: Record the deployed image reference before changing production and provide a rollback that rests on what the provider actually supports, so that a failed smoke run has an exit.

objects.title: The bootstrap credential is used once and belongs to nothing
objects.description: Define and implement how a deployment credential is discovered for an interactive first deployment, so that it is consumed in one process, never persisted, and leaves no trace of where it came from.

objects.title: Nothing secret and nothing local leaves in the image
objects.description: Automate the verification that no credential material and no developer path appears in the image, its metadata, the generated artifacts, the site output, the API documents or the deployment report.

objects.title: The image's dependencies are known and its advisories are policy
objects.description: Record what the production image contains, obtain a dependency audit and a vulnerability verdict, and state a severity and fix-availability policy so that the gate is meaningful rather than permanently red.

objects.title: Size is measured first and budgeted second
objects.description: Measure the binary, the assets, the image and the build context, declare budgets with headroom over the measured baseline, and gate unexplained growth.

objects.title: The memory hypothesis is tested, not asserted
objects.description: Run the production image under the intended memory limit, measure resident memory through a representative request sequence, and let the evidence decide the memory the deployment declares.

objects.title: Cold start and endpoint cost are benchmark targets like everything else
objects.description: Measure the cold start of the container and the cost of the cheap endpoints through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has, and record them as baselines.

objects.title: The decision is recorded where architecture decisions are recorded
objects.description: Write the architecture decision record for deploying as a generated projection of canonical deployment metadata, with the alternatives that were genuinely considered and the consequences that follow.

objects.title: Every deployment rule is a check that runs
objects.description: State the durable deployment constraints as project rules in the repository's rule system, and give each one an executable check that CI runs.

objects.title: The deployment documentation is generated and reachable
objects.description: Produce the deployment documentation from the canonical object and the implementation — architecture, container, resources, workflow, CI, security, cost, troubleshooting and scaling — and make it reachable from the surfaces that are already generated.

objects.title: The cockpit shows the deployment from the same data
objects.description: Add a deployment view to the existing cockpit that reads static policy from the canonical object and live facts from the running process, using the projection the cockpit already is.

objects.title: A pull request cannot merge a deployment that would not work
objects.description: Extend the existing verification workflow so that a pull request runs the deployment validation, the projection drift check, the production image build, the container smoke run, the resource policy assertions and the security checks.

objects.title: Production deploys from CI with a token scoped to one application
objects.description: Deploy production from CI on the repository's existing branch policy, using an application-scoped deploy token rather than an account-wide one, with concurrency that stops two pushes racing the same application.

objects.title: The real image runs under the real limits before anything is deployed
objects.description: Build the actual production image and run it under the resource limits of the cheap profile, verifying the process, its user, its port and its routes without fixed ports and without sleeping.

objects.title: The application exists, one machine runs it, and the URL answers
objects.description: Create or resolve the production application, deploy the cheap profile without accidental redundancy, verify the machine inventory and the resources against the declared policy, run the route-derived smoke suite against the public URL, and write the deployment report.

objects.title: The milestone is accepted on its evidence
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measured baselines are documented with the environment they were taken on, the workflow in the documentation runs as written, and the outcome is a plan record rather than a conversation.

objects.title: One typed graph composes the registries that already own their facts
objects.description: Extend the executable's graph derivation into a typed, deterministic model that composes the existing authoritative registries — capabilities, commands, routes, MCP exposure, skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases, benchmarks — without any of them ceasing to be authoritative.

objects.title: Relations are typed, inferred from stable identities, and never dangle
objects.description: Give the graph typed relations — implements, documents, exposes, generated from, enforced by, tested by, benchmarked by, depends on, projects to, served at — inferred where a stable convention exists, declared where it does not, and resolved or refused.

objects.title: Skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases and benchmarks enter the graph as themselves
objects.description: Bring the layer's own kinds into the graph through the registries that already index them, so that a rule, a skill, a decision, a document, a use case, a benchmark and a deployment are navigable next to the capabilities they govern.

objects.title: Availability and visibility are metadata, not conditions in a template
objects.description: Model where a capability is available — always, only in a static build, only with a running backend, only when authenticated, only at build time — and whether it is public or internal, so that every surface derives its behaviour from that rather than from its own conditionals.

objects.title: The graph is a generated artifact with a schema and no unsafe field
objects.description: Serialise the graph as a deterministic generated artifact with a schema, carrying safe metadata only, produced by the generation the repository already runs.

objects.title: The runtime reads the graph through the registry, like every other read
objects.description: Expose the graph to the running Cockpit as a declared capability, so that its route, its schema, its documentation and its benchmark coverage all follow from the declaration.

objects.title: The site renders the same graph, generated once
objects.description: Produce the static projection of the graph through the existing generation and site pipeline, so that the published site renders the same model the server does without a backend and without a second generator.

objects.title: The two projections are proved to be the same model
objects.description: Test that the static and runtime representations of the graph are equal once runtime-only fields are removed, so the published site and the running server cannot become alternate realities.

objects.title: Every menu in this repository comes from one derivation
objects.description: Derive the desktop navigation, the mobile navigation, the Cockpit sections, the documentation navigation and the landing links from one projection of the graph, with deterministic grouping and ordering.

objects.title: The overview is what exists, counted rather than claimed
objects.description: Generate the Cockpit overview and its summary numbers from the graph, showing a section only when the repository actually holds that kind of thing.

objects.title: The coverage matrix reports evidence, and never a green cell without one
objects.description: Generate a matrix showing, for every capability, whether it is documented, tested, enforced, benchmarked and exposed, where each cell resolves to an artifact or a relation rather than to a claim.

objects.title: One detail view, assembled from what a node actually has
objects.description: Render a capability's detail page from its populated sections and its resolved relations, with a stable deep link and a repository-relative reference to where the information came from.

objects.title: Search over the graph, generated, with nothing to run
objects.description: Provide one search over identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents, from a generated index that works in the static build with no service behind it.

objects.title: The relation view reads the graph and holds no data of its own
objects.description: Render the relation graph interactively from the generated data, with filters, focus, neighbour highlighting and deep links, loaded only where it is used and bounded in cost.

objects.title: A surface with no server behind it is not offered as if it had one
objects.description: Make the exposure of backend-only surfaces — the API console, live status, runtime reads — follow from availability metadata, and prove both projections behave correctly.

objects.title: The Cockpit works on a phone and before JavaScript runs
objects.description: Make the Cockpit genuinely usable at narrow viewports and keep its core information present in the served HTML, with JavaScript adding filtering, the graph, live state and search rather than being required to read anything.

objects.title: Live state is an overlay that degrades to nothing
objects.description: Let the running Cockpit overlay live state — health, peers, runtime metrics, deployment status — over the same graph, through the transport the process already has, degrading cleanly where there is none.

objects.title: The surface rules exist as checks, proved by making them fail
objects.description: State the durable constraints of this architecture as project rules with executable checks: derived surfaces stay synchronised, a public capability is discoverable, a behavioural capability carries verification, a developer-facing capability resolves to documentation, and the two projections stay equal.

objects.title: One skill runs the whole loop, and is itself in the graph
objects.description: Provide a skill that discovers capabilities, validates the graph, reports what is missing documentation, tests, exposure or enforcement, regenerates the projections and reports drift — registered, documented, tested and visible like any other.

objects.title: The graph's health is answered by the doctor that already answers everything else
objects.description: Add the graph's diagnostics to the existing health and doctor surface: the graph builds, identities are unique, relations resolve, projections are synchronised, required documentation and verification are present, and nothing unsafe is exposed.

objects.title: A browser proves the interface, at the widths people use
objects.description: Extend the existing browser checking to cover navigation on desktop and mobile, search and filtering, the detail view, graph initialisation, conditional runtime exposure, link integrity and console errors.

objects.title: Drift in any derived surface fails the build
objects.description: Extend the generation check to cover every artifact this milestone introduces — the graph, the static projection, the navigation, the indexes, the search data — so a stale committed projection cannot merge.

objects.title: Nothing private reaches a published page
objects.description: Scan the published graph, the static site and everything the client receives for credential material, private environment values and machine-absolute paths, and fail on a finding without printing it.

objects.title: The interface has a weight, and it is measured
objects.description: Measure the generated data, the served HTML, the initial scripts and styles and the graph's initialisation, and hold them to budgets through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has.

objects.title: The federated model and its two projections are an architecture decision
objects.description: Record the decision to compose the authoritative registries into one typed graph and to render it as two projections, with the alternatives that were real and the consequences that follow.

objects.title: The architecture explains itself, from inside itself
objects.description: Document the graph, its sources, its relation model, its two projections and the contributor workflow, and let the interface say how it was generated and from what.

objects.title: A synthetic capability proves the architecture instead of describing it
objects.description: Register a synthetic capability at its authoritative source alone, and prove it reaches the graph, the interface, the search, the navigation and the static projection with no other edit — and that omitting its required evidence fails enforcement.

objects.title: The inventories this replaces are removed, not left running beside it
objects.description: Find the hand-maintained inventories this architecture replaces — menus, landing cards, route lists, documentation indexes, rule and skill catalogues — and remove them, so that one derivation is the only one.

objects.title: The gate refuses what would silently break the interface
objects.description: Put the drift check, the enforcement rules, the parity test, the browser checks and the public-data scan into the existing verification workflow, so that a change leaving any derived surface stale or unsafe cannot merge.

objects.title: The milestone is accepted on its evidence
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measurements are recorded with their environment, the contributor workflow runs as written, and the remaining gaps are stated.

objects.title: The documents that explain this repository are read in a fixed order
objects.description: What to read before changing this repository, and which document answers which question.

objects.title: Milestone and DAG driven development
objects.description: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.

objects.title: A blocking question survives a handover
objects.description: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.

objects.title: A durable record names the worker that wrote it
objects.description: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.

objects.title: A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical
objects.description: A worker with no conversation history can answer what happened, why, what was decided, which evidence supports it, where the canonical source lives, and what to do next — from records and a derived index, with git still the authority over both.

objects.title: Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice
objects.description: Every public command can be benchmarked from the command registry with cold and warm distributions, the phases and work counters of any run can be printed, the caches and batch reads that remove repeated work preserve every observable result, an accepted baseline lives in the repository and a check refuses a regression by policy, and the pre-commit hook is fast enough that nobody routes around it.

objects.title: One capability graph, two projections, and no second inventory of what this repository can do
objects.description: One typed, deterministic capability graph composes the registries that already own their facts — it does not replace them — and adds typed relations between them that are inferred where a stable convention exists and declared where it does not. Both the running server and the published site render from that one graph: the static projection is the snapshot, the runtime projection is the snapshot plus live state. Navigation, overview, detail, search, the relation view and the coverage matrix are all derived, a dangling relation fails generation rather than rendering as a missing section, and a capability that exists with no documentation, no test or no enforcement is visible as such rather than indistinguishable from one that has them.

objects.title: Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data
objects.description: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.

objects.title: Execution telemetry, only from providers that expose it honestly
objects.description: Execution telemetry is recorded for providers that report it truthfully, and absence is recorded as absence rather than estimated.

objects.title: A deployment is a projection of the repository model, and a reachable URL is its evidence
objects.description: One canonical deployment object under .ai/repo/deployments/ describes the deployment; a typed Rust model parses and validates it; the container image, the Fly configuration, the smoke suite, the doctor checks, the documentation, the cockpit view and the CI jobs are all projections of that object and of the capability registry, and every one of them is checked for drift. The service runs on Fly.io on a single shared-CPU Machine that stops when idle, its health and readiness are verified from outside, the smoke suite is derived from the route registry rather than written twice, and the deployed URL answers.

objects.title: A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described
objects.description: A repository carries one policy, a small set of profiles, durable task state, and a set of commands that refuse work which does not meet a declared contract — with every rule dispatched from a registry that proves it reaches the command claiming to run it.

objects.title: Routing recommendations derived from measured cost
objects.description: The profile a task should run under is recommended from measured cost per accepted outcome, and the recommendation names the data it came from.

objects.title: Profiles become runtime constraints rather than advice
objects.description: A profile's axes become opt-in runtime clamps a provider actually applies — read size, output condensation, subagent budget — with the limit derived from the profile rather than configured twice.

objects.title: Shared policy across repositories and workers
objects.description: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.

objects.title: A worktree nobody can decide to delete
objects.description: Isolation is cheap to create and expensive to reason about: nothing records what a worktree was for or whether its work landed.

objects.title: The interface changed and its contract document did not
objects.description: A contract maintained by hand beside the code it describes goes stale on the first change that forgets it.

objects.title: A change that no plan ever asked for
objects.description: Work arrives with no bounded contract behind it, so its scope, its acceptance criteria and its ownership are all decided after the fact.

objects.title: The instruction file that grew into a rulebook
objects.description: Everything important gets appended to the always-loaded file, so every session pays for every rule and reads none of them carefully.

objects.title: A fluent contribution that could not have known the rules
objects.description: Assistants let anybody produce plausible contributions at volume; the conventions that make one correct are still only in the maintainers.

objects.title: The decision exists, in a conversation nobody can find
objects.description: A decision that was reached in a session is stored where only that session can read it, so it is neither reviewable nor discoverable.

objects.title: A hard-won discovery that never became knowledge
objects.description: A worker learns something expensive about the codebase, uses it once, and it dies with the session because nothing turned it into a durable record.

objects.title: The documented command that no longer works
objects.description: Examples are written once, in prose, and nothing ever executes them again.

objects.title: Accepting "done" because the model said so
objects.description: A fluent completion claim is accepted as evidence because nothing wrote down, beforehand, what would have to be true.

objects.title: A rule enforced by a hook that never runs
objects.description: Every artefact of enforcement exists — the rule, the script, the test — and no path connects them, so the control is fiction.

objects.title: A failure that was seen once and never again
objects.description: A failure observed inside a session is described in that session and nowhere else, so the next one starts from the report rather than the evidence.

objects.title: A capability the documentation promises and nothing proves
objects.description: A sentence describing what the software does is written once and never connected to anything that would fail if it stopped being true.

objects.title: The first hour in a repository nobody can explain quickly
objects.description: What is conventional in a codebase is knowledge held by its regulars, so every arrival — human or machine — pays for it again.

objects.title: Green tests over stale generated files
objects.description: Tests exercise the code and say nothing about the committed outputs derived from it, so the build is green and the artifacts are wrong.

objects.title: Code that quietly contradicts a written decision
objects.description: The decision was recorded and the implementation went the other way, because nothing relates a decision to the paths it governs.

objects.title: The issue says done and the repository disagrees
objects.description: Completion is recorded as a state change in a tracker rather than as evidence in the repository, so the two drift immediately.

objects.title: Nobody can reconstruct where the milestone actually is
objects.description: Progress is an aggregate that exists only in people, because the parts it aggregates were never recorded in a form anything can add up.

objects.title: Nobody can say why that worker was chosen
objects.description: Provider and model selection is made implicitly, per session, and recorded nowhere, so it cannot be reviewed or repeated.

objects.title: One worker undoing another worker's change
objects.description: A worker sees an unexplained change in its path, judges it wrong, and removes it — correctly, on the evidence it had.

objects.title: The policy changed and its four copies did not
objects.description: A decision is updated at its source and the generated copies keep serving the previous version, with nothing reporting the difference.

objects.title: Re-arguing a decision that was settled last week
objects.description: A decision whose reason lived in a conversation cannot be reviewed, only re-argued — by a worker with less information than the first one had.

objects.title: Re-explaining the same context to a brand-new session
objects.description: Repository knowledge that only ever existed in a conversation has to be re-transmitted by hand to every worker that follows.

objects.title: A result nobody can reproduce, including its author
objects.description: The result is recorded and the conditions that produced it are not, so it is an anecdote rather than a measurement.

objects.title: The rule for that directory, in a README no session ever loaded
objects.description: A local rule is either in the always-loaded file, where every session pays for it, or beside the code, where nothing relates it to the path being edited.

objects.title: The same dead end, explored twice
objects.description: Negative results are the majority of experimental output and the part nobody records, so the search space is re-explored.

objects.title: Two sessions in one checkout, standing on each other
objects.description: Two workers in one working tree see each other only as unexplained file changes, and each treats the other as noise.

objects.title: A public page promising something nothing tests
objects.description: Public material is written by a different act from the code, so it drifts ahead of the behaviour and nothing brings it back.

objects.title: Spend that cannot be tied to anything accepted
objects.description: Consumption is measured per account and outcomes are recorded per person, so the two can never be joined.

objects.title: The strongest model, at maximum effort, renaming a variable
objects.description: Capability, reasoning depth, context size and verbosity collapse into one habit — everything on — because nothing ever named them separately.

objects.title: A task "in progress" that nobody has touched for three weeks
objects.description: A status that was authored rather than computed is true at the moment of writing and decays silently from then on.

objects.title: Three copies of one explanation, and no way to tell which is current
objects.description: Every hand-maintained copy of a fact drifts on its own schedule, and a reader cannot tell which copy is the current one.

objects.title: Three roadmaps, and none of them true
objects.description: A plan kept in prose is a snapshot, and every copy of it drifts on its own schedule; stored status is an assertion that stays true after the world moves.

objects.title: Two agents fixing the same bug in two branches
objects.description: Two workers spend a day each on one defect because ownership was implicit and neither could see the other.

objects.title: Two different rulebooks for one repository
objects.description: Each provider reads its own hand-edited file, nothing relates them, and which contract applies depends on which tool is open.

objects.title: A cheap worker deciding something expensive
objects.description: Capability is dialled down for cost and nothing distinguishes the tasks where that is prudent from the ones where it is expensive.

objects.title: Asking what the workers did last night, and getting a transcript
objects.description: A conversation log records what was said, not what happened, so the operational question has to be answered by a person reading prose.

objects.title: A change whose provenance cannot be reconstructed
objects.description: Attribution stops at the commit, so what authorised a change, what verified it and what governed it are unrecoverable.

objects.title: Finished work that never reached the trunk
objects.description: Workers produce far more than integration absorbs, and nothing distinguishes work that is done from work that is done and landed.

objects.title: debugging
objects.description: reproduce, isolate, fix, and prove a defect fixed

objects.title: deep-work
objects.description: design, architecture, cross-cutting change, or a problem with no known shape

objects.title: implementation
objects.description: build a described feature or change within a known design

objects.title: routine
objects.description: small, well-understood changes; rename, bump, wording, one-line fixes

objects.title: continue
objects.description: resume a task from durable state instead of from someone's memory

objects.title: debug
objects.description: frame a defect so that the fix is proven, not asserted

objects.title: handover
objects.description: produce a continuation record body for the current task

objects.title: review
objects.description: review the working diff against the claimed scope and the finish contract

objects.title: Architecture decision integrity
objects.description: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

objects.title: AI layer integrity
objects.description: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

objects.title: Blocker resolution
objects.description: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

objects.title: Bootstrap integrity
objects.description: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

objects.title: Catalogue integrity
objects.description: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

objects.title: Checkpoint freshness
objects.description: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

objects.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
objects.description: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

objects.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
objects.description: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

objects.title: Context budget
objects.description: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

objects.title: Context integrity
objects.description: Every directory of the AI layer carries a context document, each one carries the contract, they compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

objects.title: Dependency graph integrity
objects.description: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

objects.title: Decision records
objects.description: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

objects.title: The decision threshold
objects.description: A change that is hard to reverse records the decision behind it as a decision record, and names what it put in force; an ordinary change does not.

objects.title: Define done before executing
objects.description: The finish contract is evaluated line by line, and nothing else counts as done.

objects.title: A deployment is described once, and every provider artifact is generated from it
objects.description: A deployment of the executable is a canonical object of the layer against a closed contract; the container definition and the provider configuration are projections of it, never a second description.

objects.title: Execution depth is not output verbosity
objects.description: Think as hard as the task needs; report as briefly as the profile says.

objects.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
objects.description: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

objects.title: Enforcement wiring
objects.description: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

objects.title: Externalise decisions and durable state
objects.description: A decision you make goes into a record, dated, with what was rejected and why; a question for a person goes into the questions store.

objects.title: Handover integrity
objects.description: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

objects.title: Handovers transfer state, not transcripts
objects.description: A handover says what is true now and the one next action; never conversation history.

objects.title: Parallel work requires isolation
objects.description: Do not start a second task in a checkout that already has one; overlapping claims across worktrees are reported.

objects.title: Escalate capability and effort only when justified
objects.description: The profile sets the default capability and effort; escalation is recorded, never assumed.

objects.title: Layout integrity
objects.description: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

objects.title: Ledger integrity
objects.description: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

objects.title: Load minimum sufficient context
objects.description: The profile says what to load; discover everything that may apply and load only what does.

objects.title: Note integrity
objects.description: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

objects.title: One worker, one clear scope
objects.description: A task claims the paths it may touch, and touches only those.

objects.title: Policy completeness
objects.description: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

objects.title: Policy integrity
objects.description: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

objects.title: Profile requirements
objects.description: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

objects.title: Project model integrity
objects.description: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

objects.title: Projection integrity
objects.description: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

objects.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
objects.description: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

objects.title: Prompt integrity
objects.description: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

objects.title: Questions store integrity
objects.description: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

objects.title: Retention caps
objects.description: The ledger and the handover directory stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

objects.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
objects.description: No document is a second authority for the roadmap. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.

objects.title: Rule package integrity
objects.description: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

objects.title: Every object has a schema, and the rules resolve in one stated order
objects.description: The order the rules apply in is written down rather than left in the code; every kind the tool reads declares a schema, every schema is named by a kind, and every path under the repository's AI layer is claimed by a source so that nothing is carried through unvalidated.

objects.title: Scope integrity
objects.description: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

objects.title: The episode boundary is drawn below the model, and its working context is local
objects.description: Where a provider fires session events, the episode is opened and closed by that provider's hook rather than by the model, the start event hands the worker the bounded briefing the policy declares, and the working context each open freezes stays under the ignored half of the layer, carries the declared keys, and never carries a conversation.

objects.title: Session records are shared objects with a closed field set
objects.description: A closed execution episode is written once, into the layer's sessions section, against a schema that admits what the repository can prove and nothing else.

objects.title: Sessions are workers, not memory
objects.description: Durable state lives in records the repository keeps, never in a conversation.

objects.title: Skill integrity
objects.description: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

objects.title: State consistency
objects.description: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

objects.title: Task continuity
objects.description: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

objects.title: Use-case coverage
objects.description: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

objects.title: Verification integrity
objects.description: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0; its exit code and duration are recorded.

objects.title: Verify outcomes, not activity
objects.description: A test that ran and passed is evidence; a sentence saying it did is not.

objects.title: Every public command is benchmarkable from the registry
objects.description: The benchmark targets are the public commands of share/commands.yaml and their scenarios are the command fixtures; no second list of what to time exists, and a command whose fixture the harness cannot run is a defect of the fixture, not an exemption.

objects.title: Blocking checks are deterministic and cheap
objects.description: A check that can stop a command is deterministic and cheap; work in progress is reported, never blocked.

objects.title: A cache never changes what a command observes
objects.description: A cache of derived state, if one exists, is keyed by the version of the canonical state it derives from, is bypassable, and produces byte-identical output to the uncached path; a cache that can be observed through a command's output, exit code or findings is a defect, and a cache that no case proves equivalent does not exist.

objects.title: Clean room
objects.description: The Prismatic name is the only thing carried from anywhere else: no internal paths, hostnames, component names, doctrine vocabulary or quotations.

objects.title: Context locality
objects.description: Context lives in the narrowest directory scope where it stays correct; root files bootstrap and link, provider files are projections.

objects.title: Conventional commits, committed and pushed incrementally
objects.description: Commits use the conventional format type(scope): description with the co-author footer the session provides, and land incrementally rather than as one large change.

objects.title: Derived files are regenerated, never edited
objects.description: A generated file is changed by changing its canonical source and rerunning the generator, and both are committed together; a commit that leaves the derived data behind its inputs is refused before it exists.

objects.title: Derived state is computed once per state version
objects.description: Anything derivable solely from unchanged canonical repository state is computed once per version of that state and read many times; a command's hot path does not rediscover, reparse or rebuild it per item, per request or per call.

objects.title: Distribution has one canonical model
objects.description: Supported targets, artifact names, installer resolution, the release build matrix, the documentation, the website and the exposed API metadata are derived from share/distribution.yaml or mechanically validated against it; none of them states a platform, a name or an installation URL of its own.

objects.title: English only
objects.description: Code, comments, commits, documents and governance records are written in English, with no exceptions.

objects.title: Every finding carries a reproduce command
objects.description: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it.

objects.title: A generated artifact declares its document, its encoding, its contract and its source
objects.description: Every file the generator writes declares the document it projects, the encoding it is written in, the JSON Schema its content satisfies and where it came from; it carries a provenance header in the form that encoding allows; a structured document is written in every encoding this repository commits it in from one value; and the manifest of the whole set is itself generated.

objects.title: A command reads each canonical file at most once
objects.description: Within one invocation a command flattens, hashes or parses a canonical file at most once, however many validators, accessors or projections need it; the second reader gets the first reading.

objects.title: External interfaces are projections of one capability definition
objects.description: A capability is defined once, as a typed descriptor in Rust or as a declarative object with its schema in the layer, and MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, CLI introspection and the generated reference are derived from it.

objects.title: A native command line command exists only with its documentation and its executable examples
objects.description: Every command of the Rust executable is declared once in clap with the examples beside it, every command a person can run carries at least one example that the crate's tests execute against the built binary, and the generated reference, the site dataset and the routes under /docs/cli/ are projections that CI refuses to let go stale.

objects.title: Never author identity fields
objects.description: repository_id, branch, head, working_tree and changed_files on any record are computed from git and never written by hand.

objects.title: Never store or summarise transcripts
objects.description: No record stores or summarises a conversation; records carry what is true now and the next action.

objects.title: No claim without a test
objects.description: A capability sentence in README.md or docs/ is backed by a case in test/cases/ or is phrased as a target.

objects.title: No counts in prose
objects.description: Prose never states a number the repository can compute; it states the command that computes it.

objects.title: No network, no telemetry, no eval, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion
objects.description: bin/, lib/, share/ and test/ contain no network client, no telemetry, no eval, no curl piped to a shell, no silent overwrite and no recursive deletion outside a temporary directory.

objects.title: No new nouns
objects.description: The tool gains no agents, personas, roles, tiers or registries beyond the vocabulary it has.

objects.title: Complexity is optional, not ambient
objects.description: Simple things are trivial, complex things possible, weird things hackable; a change that makes the default path harder, adds a foundational noun without a concrete need, or leaks internals into ordinary use is refused in review.

objects.title: A performance claim carries its measurement
objects.description: A change made for speed names the phase or counter it changed and both values, measured on this repository with the tool's own timing; a budget or a threshold is set from a run, never guessed; a baseline is a tracked file written by the harness and updated on purpose.

objects.title: Portable shell
objects.description: bash 3.2 and BSD userland are the floor: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no GNU-only flags, and shellcheck -x -s bash passes on every script.

objects.title: A new enforced rule is a doctrine, not an inline check
objects.description: A rule the tool enforces is declared as a rule object with an x-majordomus block and a validator named mj_validate_<name>; no command selects checks by hand.

objects.title: No endpoint of the Rust executable without a benchmark, and no number without evidence
objects.description: Every externally callable operation of the Rust executable (each executable capability directly and on every transport its exposure declares, and the transports' own operations) is a benchmark target with a denominator generated from the registry; coverage is complete or the structural check fails; a waiver is typed, reported and never counted; and a claim about latency is made from a recorded measurement, never from prose.

objects.title: One canonical declaration; modules compose capabilities; the root composes modules
objects.description: An executable capability of the Rust executable is declared once with capability!, composed into its module with module!, and the application composes modules with compose_modules!; every interface, benchmark target, cache behaviour and generated document is derived from that declaration, and editing a projection to add or change one is a defect.

objects.title: The Rust executable carries its evidence with it
objects.description: Every capability and every documented behaviour of apps/majordomus-cli is proved by a behavioural test, every public item is documented with an executable example where one is meaningful, line coverage stays above the threshold CI enforces, and the hot paths carry benchmarks.

objects.title: A command asserts in the file that declares it that it is what it claims, and is composed rather than registered
objects.description: Every capability module the executable composes carries at least one assertion that runs beside the declaration — an in-file test or an executed doc example — is reached by the root composition rather than by a registration elsewhere, and is held to a declared coverage floor.

objects.title: A request never rebuilds canonical state, and a cache is never trusted without an equivalence test
objects.description: After the Rust executable has started, no MCP or HTTP request scans the repository, builds the index or the registry, derives a schema or builds a projection; every call goes through the one executor; a cache exists only where a measurement justified it, is bounded, is keyed by the registry fingerprint, and is proved to answer what the handler answers.

objects.title: What a worker reads is declared once, and nothing outside it is read or served
objects.description: The repository scope, the pathspecs a worker reads and the paths, names, sizes and content it never reads, is declared once as data in .ai/repo/scope.yaml (or the distribution's default when a repository declares none), and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it, answers for any path whether it is in or out and why, and reports a tracked secret.

objects.title: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out
objects.description: The shared MCP server is a client's child; whatever state a client or a dead server leaves behind is taken over or bypassed, and a client that cannot share is served alone, never turned away.

objects.title: Tests run in disposable repositories
objects.description: Behavioural cases run through bash test/run.sh in a temporary repository each, never against this checkout.

objects.title: Unknown configuration keys are errors
objects.description: Every configuration file rejects a key nothing reads, and every state field is both written and read.

objects.title: A use case is proved by execution, and a capability is covered by a use case
objects.description: Every externally meaningful capability of this repository is demonstrated by an active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; every example a page shows comes from that execution; a use case's maturity is observed, never authored; and a change to a command, rule, claim, provider, MCP tool, schema, application or workflow runs use-case impact analysis before the work is called complete.

objects.title: A web surface is discovered from its producer, never registered twice
objects.description: Everything this repository exposes over HTTP is one resolved topology, discovered from producers and projected to serving, publication, validation and documentation from that one resolution.

objects.title: An operational failure mode is a catalogue object, never a page
objects.description: Every user-visible operational problem this tool answers is one schema-valid file under the layer's why section, and every listing, route, filter, count, backlink, API answer and diagnosis is derived from it; a projection that registers one is a defect.

objects.description: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

objects.title: Drift and reconciliation
objects.description: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

objects.title: Extension
objects.description: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

objects.title: Repository knowledge
objects.description: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

objects.title: Serving the layer to AI clients
objects.description: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

objects.title: Performance
objects.description: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

objects.title: Policy and enforcement
objects.description: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

objects.title: Parallel workers
objects.description: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

objects.title: Decide whether finished work is actually finished
objects.description: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

objects.title: Add a use case and let the tool prove it
objects.description: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

objects.title: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules
objects.description: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

objects.title: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered
objects.description: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

objects.title: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it
objects.description: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

objects.title: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking
objects.description: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

objects.title: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day
objects.description: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

objects.title: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data
objects.description: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

objects.title: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists
objects.description: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

objects.title: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one
objects.description: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

objects.title: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing
objects.description: A directory added under the layer without a context document fails validation by name, nothing resolves against the tree until it says what it is for, and the same hierarchy is readable over MCP and the API without running the gate.

objects.title: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it
objects.description: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

objects.title: Find an object of the layer without reading everything
objects.description: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

objects.title: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked
objects.description: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

objects.title: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one
objects.description: Read the repository''s skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

objects.title: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract
objects.description: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

objects.title: Hand unfinished work to the next session
objects.description: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

objects.title: Install the tool in one command, on a machine with no toolchain
objects.description: Paste one line, get a verified binary for this machine, and run majordomus init — no git, no Rust, no Node, no Python, no root, and no way to install an archive whose digest does not match.

objects.title: Record a decision so the next worker can find it
objects.description: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

objects.title: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget
objects.description: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

objects.title: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis
objects.description: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

objects.title: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to
objects.description: Wire the provider''s own session events, and the episode opens when the sitting begins, hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes with a continuation record beside its envelope.

objects.title: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer
objects.description: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

objects.title: Record what one worker did in one sitting
objects.description: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

objects.title: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate
objects.description: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

objects.title: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down
objects.description: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

objects.title: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression
objects.description: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

objects.title: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap
objects.description: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

objects.title: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped
objects.description: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

objects.title: See which rules apply here and what enforces them
objects.description: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

objects.title: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you
objects.description: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

objects.title: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript
objects.description: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

objects.title: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task
objects.description: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

objects.title: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding
objects.description: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

objects.title: Say what your work is for, once, and have every surface say it
objects.description: Record an operational failure mode as one file and have the command line, the API, MCP and the website answer it without registering it anywhere.

objects.title: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file
objects.description: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

objects.title: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server
objects.description: Open the repository in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

objects.title: Trace a change to the context documents it affects
objects.description: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

objects.title: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated
objects.description: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

cli.about: Majordomus control plane: a data-driven MCP server over the repository's .ai/ layer
cli.long_about:
The Rust executable of Majordomus. It reads the repository's provider-neutral AI layer under .ai/ and serves it, read-only, to MCP clients over stdio.

The task lifecycle (init, start, check, finish, doctor, ...) is the shell tool bin/majordomus in the same repository; this executable does not implement those commands.

tools.name: majordomus_artifacts
tools.title: List the generated artifacts
tools.description: The manifest `majordomus generate` commits as docs/generated/artifacts.json, reconciled with the working tree: every document with the encodings it is written in, and every file with its format, schema, source, size, hash and whether the file on disk still matches. Optionally narrowed to one document or one encoding. Reads only; `majordomus generate` writes and `majordomus generate --check` is the byte-for-byte verdict.

tools.name: majordomus_capability
tools.title: Describe one capability
tools.description: One capability by canonical id: its kind, schemas, provenance, stability, exposures, benchmark and cache policy.

tools.name: majordomus_capabilities
tools.title: List capabilities
tools.description: Every capability of this executable and this repository, summarised: kind, module, stability, provenance, the projections it declares, its benchmark and cache policy; the schemas are answered by capabilities.describe.

tools.name: majordomus_continuity
tools.title: What the lifecycle is holding
tools.description: The open episode, the active task, the handover and checkpoint that resolve for this worktree and branch, each with its divergence label, the unresolved questions that refuse completion, and the record tallies. Selection is two-tiered and never repository-wide: a record from an unrelated worktree or branch is not offered, because a briefing that is quietly about somebody else is worse than none. Absence is reported as absence.

tools.name: majordomus_deploy_check
tools.title: Would these deployments work
tools.description: Every refusal the declared deployments earn locally: a health route no capability registers, a package or binary the workspace does not produce, a build input that does not resolve, more machines running than exist, a hosted process that would bind loopback. Each names the file, the key, the value observed and the correction. Nothing here contacts the provider.

tools.name: majordomus_deployment
tools.title: One deployment
tools.description: One deployment by its identity, typed, with the repository-relative file it was read from.

tools.name: majordomus_deployments
tools.title: Deployments
tools.description: Every deployment the layer declares, typed: the application, the package and binary shipped, the address the process listens on, the routes a platform polls, the resources, the machine count, the region, the build inputs, the measured budgets and the provider's own facts. An object of the kind this executable cannot read is reported with the reason rather than skipped.

tools.name: majordomus_directories
tools.title: The layer's directory contracts
tools.description: Every directory of the layer the index knows, with the contract it declares, whether it owes one and which contract decided, and — for a named path, or when asked for everywhere — the effective chain composed from the root down, least specific first.

tools.name: majordomus_artifact
tools.title: The artifact of a target
tools.description: The archive name a target and a tag derive, the directory it unpacks into, and where a release publishes it. The one naming function answers; the release pipeline asks it rather than composing a name in a workflow file.

tools.name: majordomus_build
tools.title: This build
tools.description: What this executable is: the version of the crate it was built from, the Rust target triple, the profile, and the commit — all compiled in at build time, so an installed binary answers without a repository, a toolchain or git.

tools.name: majordomus_distribution
tools.title: The distribution model
tools.description: The one-line install command, where an installation goes, and every declared target with the artifact name it derives. This is what the installation page, the landing page's install block and the cockpit's install card render; none of them holds a platform list of its own.

tools.name: majordomus_releases
tools.title: Published releases
tools.description: Every release this repository recorded, newest first, and the one an unpinned installation resolves to: the highest version among the stable, unwithdrawn records. The pointer is derived here and never authored anywhere.

tools.name: majordomus_graph
tools.title: Derive one graph
tools.description: One graph by id: its nodes and edges with the vocabularies that say what each kind means, the file every node was derived from, and whether the result is acyclic. Deterministic for a given tree and executable.

tools.name: majordomus_graphs
tools.title: List graphs
tools.description: Every graph this executable derives: its id, what it shows, and what it is derived from.

tools.name: majordomus_health
tools.title: Health of this process
tools.description: Every dimension of what this process serves — the layer as it was read, the registry, the scope, version control, benchmark coverage, the committed registry manifest and the attached peers — each decided by the engine that owns it, with the command that reproduces the verdict.

tools.name: majordomus_get
tools.title: Get one object
tools.description: One object by URI (majordomus://<kind>/<identity>): metadata, provenance and content; a URI a query projects (majordomus://repository) answers that query as a JSON document. The same resolution serves the MCP resource read.

tools.name: majordomus_list
tools.title: List objects
tools.description: List the declarative objects of the repository's AI layer, optionally by kind or tag.

tools.name: majordomus_search
tools.title: Search objects
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search over identities, titles, descriptions and content.

tools.name: majordomus_announce
tools.title: Announce what this peer is working on
tools.description: Tell the other peers of this shared server what the calling session is doing and which paths it expects to touch. Changes this process's memory only; the repository is never written. Needs an MCP session: over plain HTTP there is no caller.

tools.name: majordomus_peers
tools.title: List peers
tools.description: Every client attached to this shared server: id, the client's own name and version from its initialize, transport, when it attached, when it was last seen, and what it announced. In-memory, gone with the process.

tools.name: majordomus_perf
tools.title: Performance counters
tools.description: The counters of this process: repository scans, index and registry builds, schema generations, projection builds, executions, handler invocations, cache hits, misses and evictions, and the phase timings, as they stand now.

tools.name: majordomus_repository
tools.title: Repository and index state
tools.description: The repository root, layer sections, git state, discovery mode, kinds present, every diagnostic, and the capability registry counted.

tools.name: majordomus_scope
tools.title: The repository scope
tools.description: The scope declaration as read, where it came from (the repository's own or the distribution's default), and every tracked file tallied against it: how many are in, how many are out for each reason, and which.

tools.name: majordomus_scope_classify
tools.title: Judge a path against the scope
tools.description: Whether a repository-relative path is in or out of the scope, the reason when it is out, and the pattern or limit that decided; an existing file is judged by name, then size, then content.

tools.name: majordomus_why_areas
tools.title: Operational areas
tools.description: Every operational area the catalogue declares, each with the public moments that fall under it. Membership is derived from the moments and is never listed in an area's own file.

tools.name: majordomus_why_audiences
tools.title: Audiences
tools.description: Every audience the catalogue declares, each with the public moments that name it. Membership is derived from the moments and is never listed in an audience's own file.

tools.name: majordomus_why_diagnose
tools.title: Diagnose a selection
tools.description: What a reader's own symptoms imply: the moments the selection resolves to, the operational areas and audiences they weigh towards, and the capabilities, commands, claims, rules and use cases that answer them — each carrying the moments that produced it. Counting, not inference: there is no weighting and no percentage.

tools.name: majordomus_why
tools.title: The catalogue
tools.description: Every operational moment this repository holds, narrowed by any of the facets the catalogue itself reports, with the audiences, the areas, the derived filters and the counts. The default is the public catalogue; pass status=any for the drafts too.

tools.name: majordomus_why_moment
tools.title: One moment
tools.description: One operational moment in full: what it looks like, why it happens, what it costs, what this tool does about it, and every relation derived from its metadata — the responsibilities its claims belong to, the moments that name it, and the moments nearest it by shared area, audience and tag.

tools.name: majordomus_why_validate
tools.title: Validate the catalogue
tools.description: Every finding over the catalogue: a reference that resolves to nothing, with the nearest candidate; a duplicate identity; a file name that disagrees with its id; and a public record that does not meet the floor its status promises. Errors make the catalogue invalid; warnings do not.
